title: Bangladesh gets under $0.5bn a year from abroad for adaptation
excerpt: It needs $8.5 billion a year for adaptation and pays 88% from its own budget, a COP31 side event heard.
content:
Bangladesh needs about US$8.5 billion a year for climate adaptation but has around $4 billion, and less than $0.5 billion of that comes from international sources, according to figures presented at a COP31 side event in Antalya, Türkiye, on Wednesday, 11 November. The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) released the figures on 12 November.

The event, "Climate Change Adaptation in Bangladesh: From National Success to Global Scale-Up", was held at the Bangladesh Pavilion by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and UNDP.

Key figures

  • Annual adaptation need: about $8.5 billion.
  • Available now: around $4 billion a year, of which under $0.5 billion is international.
  • Paid at home: nearly 88% of adaptation spending comes from the national budget.
  • Tracking: climate spending is tracked across 25 ministries and divisions.
  • Early warning: more than 4,200 cyclone shelters and over 76,000 volunteers who carry warnings. A single cyclone in 1991 killed close to 140,000 people.

All figures are as given in the UNDP press release. Devlens has not seen the underlying government estimate. At a separate delegation briefing on 13 November, officials put Bangladesh's total climate need, not only adaptation, at $10 billion to $11 billion a year.

Who said what

Shaikh Faridul Islam, State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, said "adequate, predictable and grant-based climate finance is essential to scale up Bangladesh's adaptation success", according to UNDP. Prof S M Abdul-Awal, Principal Coordinator (SDG Affairs) at the Prime Minister's Office, said "adaptation is development" and that progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is not secure without it.

Panellists included Ulrika Åkesson of the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) and Dr Daouda Ndiaye of the Islamic Development Bank. The release does not report what they said.

Women and climate finance

At a separate Bangladesh Pavilion event on gender-responsive climate finance, held with UN Women Bangladesh, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said safety, mobility and the participation of women "must be built into adaptation by design, not added as afterthoughts". Her remarks were reported by Daily Waadaa from a Ministry of Foreign Affairs press release, which says the event took place on Thursday.

Why it matters

The numbers put a figure on the gap behind Bangladesh's call for grants rather than loans. If international money stays under $0.5 billion a year, most adaptation work will keep relying on the national budget and on NGO and community programmes funded project by project. NGOs bidding for adaptation funds may find donors asking for gender and locally led design as standard.

What to watch

Whether the COP31 cover text sets any baseline or share for adaptation finance, after the plan to triple it was kept off the formal agenda. The talks close on 20 November.
